BlaÅ¾ys / LRT A company linked to Lithuanian technology and investment group Tesonet has applied for regulatory approval to acquire Grand Hotel Vilnius, a landmark hotel located near Cathedral Square in the capital, the Competition Council said. Netherlands-based Spectra, which is associated with Tesonet Global holding company, submitted a request to acquire 100% of the shares in the company that operates the hotel. The application was filed July 27, according to the regulator. Grand Hotel Vilnius is currently owned by a subfund of investment management company I Asset Management, according to data from the Centre of Registers. The hotel, located in central Vilnius, operated under the name Grand Hotel Kempinski Vilnius until May 2024. In late 2023, the hotel signed a franchise agreement with international hospitality group Hilton and a management agreement with Apex Alliance Hotel Management. It began operating as Grand Hotel Vilnius, Curio Collection by Hilton, on May 17, 2024. In August 2024, the IAM Grand Hotel Vilnius subfund of I Asset Management became the hotelâs sole shareholder. Grand Hotel Vilnius reported revenue of 6.96 million euros last year, up 10.6% from the previous year, while its net loss narrowed 2.2 times to 638,000 euros, according to financial statements submitted to the Centre of Registers. The company said the hotel plans to invest more than 10 million euros in renovations, including upgrades to conference rooms, guest rooms, the facade, gym and lobby. Most of the work is expected to be completed by the end of 2026. Because half of the hotelâs rooms will be unavailable throughout the renovation period, the company forecasts a 40% occupancy rate and revenue of 5 million euros in 2026. Photograph: Nepal Army/AP Nepal-Tibet flood disaster Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flood disaster Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation William Christou Sat 5 Sep 2026 07.26 EDT Last modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 07.38 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Emergency responders rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations on Saturday, as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal . The Nepali military said a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel. Rescue efforts have focused on a dozen hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing, 500 of whom are thought to be trapped in huge tunnels. International rescue teams from India, China , South Korea and the US have been searching through debris and damaged structures at the projects to try to find survivors. Two Nepali workers were rescued from another tunnel in a hydro-station on the Trishuli River on Friday. Rescue of Nepal hydropower workers ‘triumph for humans and humanity’, tunnelling expert says Read more Experts have said that as time passes, the possibility of finding missing people alive in the tunnels is diminishing. The Nepali woman, 64, was rescued from a damaged house in the devastated town of Nuwakot. Photos published by the Nepali army showed rescuers discovering the woman submerged in mud before she was pulled to safety and airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment. Members of Nepal’s police force cheered as she was pulled from the home, the lower half of which was buried in thick sludge. Emergency responders have been working to find survivors from the devastating floods in Nepal, which were triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on 26 August. Their work has been complicated by the massive infrastructural damage caused by the floods, with more than 40 bridges having collapsed and rivers swelling unpredictably. At least 1,375 people have been killed in the floods, with more than 5,000 missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.
